chunks: Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAbdillah, peace be upon them, were asked about a man who has a house, a servant, and a slave: may he accept zakat?
They said: “Yes. Indeed, the house and the servant are not wealth.”

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Jaʿfar, Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir عليه السلام
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu ʿAbdillah, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: zakat, the obligatory alms that may be received by eligible persons
key_terms.مَالٍ: wealth or property counted as financial means

ai.seo_question: Can a person who owns a house and a servant still receive zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a person may still receive zakat even if he possesses a house and a servant. In this context, such necessities are not treated as qualifying wealth that would prevent him from accepting zakat.
